div.div: 2 فلّذ , (T, L,) inf. n. تَفْلِيذٌ; (T, O, L, K;) as also ↓ فَلَذَ , inf. n. فَلْذٌ; (L, TA;) He cut in pieces (T, O, L, K) flesh-meat. (T, L.) Hence, in a trad., كَبِدَهُ ↓ إِنَّ الفَرَقَ مِنَ النَّارِ فَلَذَ [Verily the fear of the fire of Hell cut in pieces his liver; but perhaps فَلَذَ is here a mistranscription for فَلَّذَ]; said, by the Prophet, of one who had died from fear of the fire [of Hell]. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
